sentences.sentence: "It flew by quicker than I could comprehend.
The only thing I could see is the same bored face that the man had.
It was the saddest thing I'd ever seen in my life so far.
The common factor in this man's whole life is he had that same bored face.
Then he comes out and says he has seen in his whole life in this one time in the chair.
Can you imagine that?
To live a whole life in just one time.
The man looks like he is so happy when he comes out, he nearly jumps out of his skin.
He says he would like to go again, that it was so good.
I think it's a bad thing, a terrible thing, for to have to see what is going to be at the end of it.
that' tell you to come back again.
"Well, I went back.
I went back too, I have been back now for a lot of years, now.
I am getting so that I look forward to it.
I like to go and sit down in the chair and close my eyes and see.
I see things that I like and things that I don't like, but I see them all, I see them all.
When I am in the machine I am not me.
I am somebody else then.
I'are not afraid of anything when I'm in the machine.
I have seen so many lives now, I know all about life.
Please don't go in the chair.
Don't go in the old man's chair.
The man is dead now.
I think he has been dead a long time now.
But his chair is still there, and I go back in it and go and see some more lives.
I don't know where I am going to go when I die.
I dont know how I will get there.
I do know, though.
The words on the letter tremble slightly as I try and read.
'If not, you should complain to the package - I paid good money to make sure this got there on time.'
The letter is on plain thin paper, the kind you get for nothing at the store, and it is all scribbled in pencil, just like my brother used to write.
I haven't seen his writing in nearly seventeen years, not since he died.
I go to the kitchen, get a chair and set it by the woodstove, because it' mabe i am not too old to learn to see straight, it's not that, it's that the little room all looks the same.
I set the letter there by the stove, then I go out and sit down in the chair by the front of the house and watch the sun go down.
When the sun is all gone and the moon is up, I go in and I put the light on and get the chair that is by the woodstove and sit down there and read the rest of the letter.
I look at the words, but they don't make any sense to me.
I know it's his writing, but I can't make out what he is saying.
He says, 'I am sending you a package.
It will come in a few days.
I think you need it.'
It is not much of a letter, but it is all I got from him.
A few days go by and a man comes to the door and wants to know if I know a man called Harry.
The man goes away and I don't know what he means.
The next day, the man comes back.
I ask him what he wants.
It started like any other Saturday.
I was sitting at my normal table outside of my favorite cafe, The Hole.
Weird name, I know.
I've learned not to question it.
I read the paper as I wait for my friend Charlie comes every Saturday, we have coffee and talk for a little while.
That's how it has been for years.
But this Saturday was different.
There was this couple sitting across the street, sitting on a bench and they are arguing.
They are getting madder and madder, and you can see they both are really mad.
The man is standing up now, and the girl is crying.
I don't know what they's arguing about.
I didn't want to get mixed up in it.
so I keep on reading my paper, but I look up every now and then to see what is going on.
The man is holding his hand up like this, like he is going to hit the girl, and the girl, she just keeps on crying.
Then the man throws the thing down on the bench and walks away, and the girl just sit there and cry some more.
I finish my coffee and pay and go inside.
I go up to the counter and tell the owner, "Joe, that couple over there, they are going to hurt each other."
Joe, he just looks at me and he says, "That's none of your business."
I went outside again and the police are there now.
they took the man away.
The little girl she still is there and she is crying.
I think she is all alone now.
I wish I could do something to help her.
Next day, I go back to the cafe.
I go up to the counter and order a coffee, but when the coffee is ready, I put some money on the counter, and I get up and go to the door.
I don't know why I did that.
"The light!
The light, it hurts, it hurts!"
Or rather, he thought he said it, but there wasn't any way to know, there was no way to know anything, except that he was here and the light hurts.
He was sure he was dead.
He had died.
He looked up to where there was not any up, and down there was not any down.
He closes his eyes, that's what I do when the light hurts.
The light doesn't hurt now.
Good.
He open his eyes again.
Then he sees it.
Or maybe he just sees what he thinks it is.
There is a man there.
A man in a coat.
A long coat that goes to his feet, and he has a long white beard, like a beard a man would have in a picture in a book.
I am in heaven, John thinks.
I am in heaven, and that is good, because that is what I always thought I should be.
But then he sees the other one.
She is sitting on the floor.
She is a woman, and she is crying.
He knows it is his wife.
She does not know he is there.
"Oh, God," she says.
"I can not go on.
I can't go on, oh, God, I can not go on."
John knows she will go now.
He knows she will go and be with God, and he will have to stay here alone.
He will stay here and die all the time.
"You can come up here," he say.
She look at him.
"You can come up here and sit by me," he say.
She looks up at him and she says "Oh, John, John, John!
I am so glad you are here."
She comes up to him and puts her hand in his.

my name is called  Tacey, and I am a man, but I am tired too.

and the other folks in the family they hold to the old man, and we all jump together.
we go down in the water.

He picked himself out of bed and ventured to the bathroom where he would brush his teeth with the same tasting toothpaste that he's always used, take a look at himself in the glass, shave with the same kind of razor he's always used, and wear the same kind of clothes he's always worn.
I don't think I need to tell you what kind of things he does, because it's all so like what ever anybody else does.
That is until this morning.
This morning when he looked at his watch and sees it's six o' knowe, he just sits down on the edge of the bed and he does not get up again.
Now, you know I can't make it seem very good, but if you want to know what happened, it is like that.
It was on Monday, and it was very cold, and he felt very bad, and the reason he felt so bad is because he was going to kill himself.
